Class DailyListeningStatsService

java.lang.Object
com.sebastiandorata.musicdashboard.service.handlers.DailyListeningStatsService
@Service public class DailyListeningStatsService extends Object
Provides daily and weekly listening statistics for the dashboard stat cards.

Recording path

  1. The browser plays a song through its HTML5 audio element. The server-side MusicPlayerService (one instance per browser session) keeps the queue and tracking flags.
  2. After 20 seconds of playback the browser calls POST /api/player/tracked. The endpoint creates the PlaybackHistory row, with playedAt set to LocalDateTime.now().
  3. When the track ends, the browser calls POST /api/player/ended. The row is marked completed and its duration is set to the full track length.

playedAt is stored with no zone. On a UTC server the value is UTC wall-clock time; on a developer machine in Toronto it is Eastern time. The database holds whatever the server's local clock said at that instant. Only plays of at least 20 seconds count as valid.

Retrieval path

  1. DashboardController renders the dashboard page. The stat cards are refreshed by a browser call to /api/dashboard/stats.
  2. The stats request runs on the request thread and calls buildStatSnapshot(), which returns the snapshot directly. No background loader and no UI thread are involved.
  3. buildStatSnapshot() takes the logged-in user ID from UserSessionService and queries PlaybackHistoryRepository.findByUserIdOrderByPlayedAtDesc(userId), returning all of that user's rows, newest first.
  4. Each row's playedAt is converted to Toronto local time by toTorontoTime(LocalDateTime). The day and week boundaries are also computed in Toronto time using LocalDate.now(TORONTO), so both sides of the comparison use the same zone.
  5. The filtered lists are passed to the compute helpers, which build the StatSnapshot.
  6. Session duration comes from UserSessionService.getSessionDurationSeconds(). It is computed in memory as now minus the login time, so it involves no database call.

Time conversion

playedAt is stored with no zone. On a UTC server, a song played at 23:30 Toronto time is stored as 04:30 the next UTC day. Without the conversion, LocalDate.now() on a UTC server returns the UTC date, so the filter window is wrong and misses plays from 19:00 to 23:59.

After the conversion, stored values are re-interpreted as Toronto time before comparison, so the window is effectively: Toronto-23:59.

Time Complexity: O(n). One DB fetch + O(n) in-memory stream passes.

Space Complexity: O(n) for the fetched list.

  • Method Details

    • buildStatSnapshot

      public StatSnapshot buildStatSnapshot()
      Builds all stat-card values from a single database fetch.

      Retrieval path summary:

      1. Fetch all rows for this user from playback_history ordered newest-first (one query).
      2. Convert each playedAt from system zone to Toronto time via toTorontoTime(LocalDateTime).
      3. Partition into todayPlays and weeklyPlays using Toronto-time boundaries.
      4. Derive all stats from those in-memory sublists. No extra queries.
      5. Session duration read from UserSessionService.getSessionDurationSeconds() No DB call, in-memory subtraction (now - sessionStart).
      Returns:
      a fully populated StatSnapshot; never null
